subject: Request: interim coverage statement for SOC 2 period transition
messages:
From: Priya Singh <psingh@novacorp.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: interim coverage statement for SOC 2 period transition

Hi Sean,

Quick follow-up from our procurement run here — we received Redwood's SOC 2 Type II for the period ending 2027-06-30, thank you. Our audit and procurement teams are asking for an interim coverage statement (sometimes called a bridge letter or short-term attestation) to cover the window between the report end date and the date of contract signing. Specifically they want confirmation that there were no control deviations in the controls covered by the SOC 2 during the period 2027-07-01 to current date.

Can Redwood provide: 1) a short signed interim coverage statement (one page is fine), 2) a list of the evidence types you can share for that period (e.g., SOC log extracts, KMS access logs, change control summary), and 3) an estimated turnaround (we're aiming to complete approval by 2027-08-25).

I've attached our procurement checklist to show what our security team will validate. Our external auditors (AuditPartner LLP) will accept either a signed Redwood interim statement or a bridge letter from your auditors if that's easier.

Thanks,
Priya Singh
Senior Security Program Manager
Novacorp
Attachment: audit_request_checklist.xlsx
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <psingh@novacorp.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: interim coverage statement for SOC 2 period transition

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear note and checklist. We can support this. A few clarifying points so we align on scope:

- Report: SOC 2 Type II, period ending 2027-06-30 (confirmed).
- Coverage requested: controls in scope of that report for 2027-07-01 through the current date.
- Delivery options: we can provide a Redwood-signed interim coverage statement (company attestation) and a short evidence package (logs and high-level control affirmation). Alternatively, our external auditor can provide a bridge letter, but that route takes longer (coordination with our auditor and scheduling).

What we'll need from you to prepare the short attestation:
- Confirmation whether AuditPartner will accept a Redwood internal attestation OR must it be from the auditor.
- Any specific control families you want highlighted (e.g., change management, access controls, encryption/KMS) beyond the standard in-scope list.

Estimated timeline if you accept a Redwood attestation: 1) we prepare a draft interim statement and evidence list (2 business days), 2) internal sign-off with security & legal (up to 3 business days), 3) return signed PDF via DocuSign. So optimistic turnaround ~5 business days once we have your confirmation.

I've attached an initial draft (v1) internally — Naomi/Karthik, please see below for technical evidence we can include and confirm.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: interim coverage statement for SOC 2 period transition

Sean / Karthik — drafting notes and evidence we can provide for the 2027-07-01 -> present window: 

- Logs: condensed token-level request logs (aggregate counts, not PII), API access logs for the Novacorp tenant (time range filter), and KMS key rotation events.
- Configuration: exported IAM role bindings and service account changes for the Novacorp dedicated/tenant ID.
- Change management: a short linear log of deploys and schema migrations affecting inference runtime (dates, owners, high-level description).
- Incidents: none to report in that window; we'll include the incident statement and add cross-reference IDs.

Attachments: draft_interim_statement_v1.pdf (internal draft; includes proposed language: "Redwood Inference affirms, to the best of its knowledge and based on available records, that controls in scope of the SOC 2 Type II report remained operational and no material control deviations were identified for the period 2027-07-01 through [CURRENT_DATE].")

One legal note: we should avoid categorical "no incidents" language without qualifying data; propose "no known material deviations". Karthik, please review wording for legal comfort; if we need auditor-signed bridge language we'll surface that to Sean.

— Naomi
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <psingh@novacorp.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2027 11:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: interim coverage statement for SOC 2 period transition

Hi Priya — attaching the revised interim coverage statement (v2) and a one-page evidence checklist. Per Naomi and legal review, language has been softened to "no known material deviations."

What you can expect next:
1) You confirm AuditPartner's acceptance of a Redwood-signed interim attestation.
2) We initiate DocuSign and share the signed PDF.
3) We package the evidence bundle (redacted logs, rotation events, deploy list) via a secure S3 link and share an access token; AuditPartner can validate items as needed.

Links and refs: DocuSign (pre-sign): https://app.docusign.com/doc/ABC1234XYZ 
HubSpot record: HS-00982345

Attachment: draft_interim_statement_v2_signed.pdf (pre-signed by security; final signature pending)
